name: tracker
description: What is being kept up, at a glance: each habit against its target for this day or week, its streak, the last days as dots, and a press to log. From the habit and entry records, kept current. At glance detail it is how many are met today.

use.when: a person keeps something up and wants to see and log it without thinking: habits, a daily measure, a weekly distance.
use.not: a one-off task, which is a task; or numbers over time on their own, which is a chart.
use.with: the habit records behind it, each with its own page, numbers and chart.

detail.title: How much to show
detail.description: glance is how many are met this period, for a corner. full is every habit with its bar, streak, days and Log.

tags.description: Show only habits with one of these tags. Leave out for all that are not archived.

habits.description: The habits as they stand. Filled in by the server from the records.

progress.description: In words: 3 of 8 glasses, done, not yet.

pct.description: This period against the target, 0 to 100.

goal.description: Progress on a longer goal, in words; empty for none.

keyboard.does: reaches each habit's name, the amount field when it has a unit, and Log

wcag.notes: A named region. Each bar is a progressbar with its value, its target and a name that says both in words, so the picture is never the only way to read it. The streak and each day dot carry their meaning in words for a reader. Log is a plain form that works without scripts. Colour marks a met day, and the word does too.

machine.identify: Each habit is a list item with data-id and data-met; the progressbar carries aria-valuenow and aria-valuemax; the streak is .sw-tracker__streak.
machine.operate: To log, fill the amount (when there is one) and activate Log, which POSTs to /habit/{id}/log. The same is create_record on entry with the habit's id.
